_design_note: F1, the solo candidate for submission. Two results combine here and have never been run together: M3.10 showed that at (128, 64) the learning rate has to come down with the width -- at 5e-4 it matches the control on score with resolvably fewer suicides (0.171 against 0.453, non-overlapping across seeds) and the lowest death rate the project has measured (6.4 per thousand bombs against 15.9) -- and M3.9 showed that with the schedule pinned in absolute rounds a 5000-round budget is worth +2.43 on loot-crate, which is not resolvable but is not a loss either. The open question this arm answers: a wider net at half the step size takes the same ~111k updates in 2000 rounds as the narrow one, so it may simply be undertrained there. Every budget arm so far has been run at (64, 32) and 1e-3. Updated to R02_8: double_dqn is carried into the solo candidate too. Section 7.24.3 found it adds nothing measurable in solo once the step size is right (M3.14 6.6 deaths per thousand bombs against M3.10's 6.4), so this arm is expected to track M3.14 rather than beat it; keeping one route across both candidates is what makes F1 and F2 differ in the opponents alone.

Re-run scripts/diagnose_bomb_escape.py and compare against M3.10's 155 deaths / 24,245 bombs / 46 with a plan throughout. Report deaths per thousand bombs, not the WAIT rate: across four arms the WAIT rate moves opposite to the death rate.
